context_quotes:
- **Resilience** — when resilience is required, prefer `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` for HttpClient and `Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience` for general pipelines (D-12). Do not add the deprecated `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly` or `Polly.Extensions.Http`; a direct Polly reference or Polly API configuration is an explicit exception that needs a documented reason why the Microsoft.Extensions APIs cannot express the requirement.
- **API versioning** — when Controller API versioning has been explicitly adopted (D-15), use the Controller integration of `Asp.Versioning` (for example `Asp.Versioning.Mvc` with `Asp.Versioning.Mvc.ApiExplorer`); do not add it before the project actually adopts versioning.
- **Validation** — `FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions` for registration; do not add a deprecated or legacy ASP.NET automatic-validation integration package without a concrete requirement (D-05).

New `HttpClient` per request; mandating one client model everywhere; retrying unsafe operations without idempotency analysis; unbounded retries; leaking `HttpResponseMessage` across boundaries; ignoring cancellation; dynamic tokens in shared default headers; mapping every upstream failure to the same status; resilience pipelines added without understanding them.

Resilience policies match failure and operation semantics; add a mechanism only for an identified failure scenario, and observe retries, timeouts and circuit state when they matter operationally. The Microsoft packages are built on Polly v8, but application code uses the `Microsoft.Extensions` resilience APIs.

The standard handler is useful when its behavior fits the remote API; it is not mandatory for every client. Review its retry behavior carefully for state-changing requests, and avoid stacking handlers with overlapping strategies.

Do not wrap normal EF Core operations in a generic application-level retry pipeline. When the provider supports transient retry through EF Core execution strategies or provider configuration, prefer that, and handle transaction/retry interaction according to the provider's EF Core guidance. HTTP retry policies are not database policies.

| Scenario | Consideration |
|---|---|
| External I/O | Bounded execution time |
| Safe transient HTTP failure | Consider retry |
| Unsafe write | No retry unless duplicate-safe |
| `429` from dependency | Honor `Retry-After` where appropriate |
| Repeated dependency outage | Consider circuit breaker |
| Optional data unavailable | Consider explicit fallback |
| Latency-sensitive idempotent read | Consider hedging after measurement |
| EF transient faults | Provider/EF execution strategy |
| Incoming request rate limiting | ASP.NET Core rate limiter |
The `Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch` package is deprecated; use the official `Elastic.Serilog.Sinks` package (same `WriteTo.Elasticsearch` name, ECS documents to data streams):

- `Services` — Application Services and useful public service contracts: `ITaskService.cs`, `TaskService.cs`. No handler, CQRS or MediatR structures.
- `DTOs` — Application-level operation/data models when useful; not a dumping ground.

canonical_policy.name: Modern Serilog integration is the baseline
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: When Serilog is configured, use the modern DI-integrated AddSerilog approach and keep provider configuration in environment-aware configuration; application code continues to depend on ILogger<T>.

reviews.boundary_analysis: DI-integrated/configaware/ILogger matches. DirectSerilog boundary, conditionalbootstrap and staticloggerflush with purelyhostmanaged exception independently captured. DefaultstrengthBF0094 retained.

context_quotes:
- Default: `ILogger<T>` with structured message templates and stable property names; avoid string interpolation that turns structured values into opaque text.
- Default: when Serilog is configured, use the DI-integrated `AddSerilog` approach with provider configuration in environment-aware configuration; application code keeps depending on `ILogger<T>`.

String interpolation in log calls; duplicate exception logging; expected outcomes logged as errors; credentials or secrets in logs; whole objects dumped without review; provider-specific APIs spread through Application code; logs used as an audit database without a dedicated audit design.

Integration rule: `rules/backend/hosting.md` § Logging. Application code keeps using `ILogger<T>`; direct Serilog APIs (`Log.Logger`, `LogContext`) stay at composition or provider-specific boundaries.

`AddSerilog()` integrates with DI (`ReadFrom.Services`), replacing the older `builder.Host.UseSerilog()`.

Use a bootstrap logger when startup failures before DI/configuration need to be captured; simpler applications can skip it.

When the static/bootstrap `Log.Logger` is used, flush it on shutdown (`try`/`finally` with `CloseAndFlushAsync`) so buffered events from asynchronous sinks are written; purely host-managed logging follows the provider's lifetime.

Keep levels, sinks and overrides in configuration so they can differ per environment. The example shows several optional sinks at once — File, Seq and others are not baseline dependencies; a Console sink suffices for a simple local Development baseline, and numeric limits and retention values are illustrative.

| Scenario | Technique |
|---|---|
| Serilog as provider | `AddSerilog()` + configuration |
| Development log storage | Seq (free single-user) or Aspire Dashboard |
| Production log storage | Seq, Elasticsearch (Elastic sink) or an OTLP backend |
| Request logging | `UseSerilogRequestLogging()` |
| Scoped properties | `LogContext.PushProperty()` in middleware |
| Expression-based filtering | `Serilog.Expressions` |
| Audit trail | `AuditTo` (synchronous, exceptions propagate) |
| Levels per environment | `MinimumLevel.Override` in appsettings |
| OpenTelemetry integration | `Serilog.Sinks.OpenTelemetry` |
